alternatives.concept: A qualified UCR response combines substantive programming, databases, mathematics, probability, statistics, data science and machine learning with accounting, finance, economics, marketing and AI governance. These whole courses offer related analytical tools and business context. They do not reproduce Maastricht’s recurring eLab business-data projects, operations and supply-chain curriculum, restricted disciplinary menus, R/web skills, study abroad, 13 EC analytics project or 8 EC individual thesis. The sustainability partner project adds genuine applied teamwork in another domain.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum is dominated by UCR's data science, AI, mathematics and computer-science cluster (14 of 24 courses: Introduction to Programming, Mathematical Methods, Introduction to Data Science, Linear Algebra, Probability & Statistics, Machine Learning, Neural Networks & Deep Learning, Database Management Systems, AI Ethics, Decision-making in AI, Optimization Methods in AI, Computational & Numerical Methods, Algorithms & Data Structures, and Research Methods & Statistics), complemented by a substantial business, economics and finance cluster (Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations, Introduction to Economics, Business & Economy in the Age of AI, Accounting & Corporate Finance, Money Banking & Finance, Marketing & Consumer Engagement, Market Research, Econometrics) and one team research project. A single-field label such as Data Science would hide the business half of the programme, and a Business label would hide its technical majority, so the label names both strands and the decision focus.

progressionAssessment.rationale: DISGATE101 (semester 1) and DISGATE102 and BENGATE102 (semester 2), none of which has a prerequisite, precede every course that formally requires them: DISARIN211 and DISCOMP311 (semester 5) and DISARIN311 (semester 6) require DISGATE101; DISMATH314 and DISMATH211 (semester 3) and DISMATH213 and DISDATA311 (semester 4) require DISGATE102; BENENTR211 (semester 4) and BENECON312 (semester 6) require BENGATE102; and BENBUSI312 and BENENTR311 (semester 6) require BENGATE101 (semester 1). Advisory progression is followed where feasible: Introduction to Programming and Introduction to Data Science are in semester 1; probability and statistics, linear algebra and Machine Learning (semester 3) follow Mathematical Methods (semester 2) and precede Neural Networks & Deep Learning (semester 4), Econometrics (semester 6) and Optimization Methods in AI (semester 6, after Decision-making in AI in semester 5); Accounting & Corporate Finance (semester 5) precedes Money, Banking & Finance (semester 6); and Marketing & Consumer Engagement (semester 4) precedes Market Research (semester 6). Personal & Professional Development is in semester 1.

alternativeSelection.assessment: One substantive integrated alternative retained after reading all24actualfullprofiles andweights. Businessfunctions already have accounting/finance/marketing/econometrics/economics/marketresearch andAIbusiness context. Additional actual Microeconomics and Behavior, Behavioral Economics and Strategy/DigitalTransformation support refinements, but do not establish four distinct additional target-specific courses without replacing defining analytics content with generic business breadth. Mathematical/dataengineering/deeplearning/research choices are now genuine restricted menus, not mandatory additional core; the existing technical foundation already includes14courses. Additional unrelated robotics/advanced differential-equation or generic legal/leadership content cannot be justified as filling the defining target methods. A standalonegovernance direction lacks sustained technical/legaldataengineering scope. Rejection is substantive,not merely coherence or a numericalquota. Three isamaximum,notatarget. Applied organisational-data cases and independent analytics research (5649/5651) are not owned by the retained direction: ENSSUST313 is a contextual sustainability project and optional research is additional, so neither establishes the defining repeated business-data case and individual analytics-thesis sequence. A separate project-led candidate is unsupported by the available UCR course base.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Business & Economy in the Age of AI provides a partial contribution to an important and identifiable part of Introduction to Business Analytics' subject, how business and data or AI connect, including AI's capabilities and limits, privacy and ethics through business cases; it does not teach the introductory data-analytic techniques (clustering, prediction, visualisation) or the group case project of that component.

Mathematical Methods provides a partial contribution to the calculus and mathematical-modelling half of Mathematics and Statistics 1 (differentiation, integration and applied modelling projects); its statistics half (descriptive statistics, probability and sampling) is covered by other UCR courses on separate rows.

Linear Algebra provides a partial contribution to the linear-algebra half of Mathematics and Statistics 2 (matrices, systems of linear equations, vector spaces and transformations); the statistical-inference half is covered by other UCR courses on separate rows.
Introduction to Programming provides related taught content for the target's Fundamentals of Programming: Python, data types, control structures, and the steps from problem to implemented programme.

Database Management Systems provides related taught content for relational database design, SQL querying and query processing, the core of the target's Database Management; its managerial and non-relational topics are not specifically covered.

Search, constraint satisfaction and optimisation projects include linear and nonlinear programming. This is a partial computational contribution, not the complete target modelling curriculum, integer programming, maximum-flow, simplex and business-specific techniques.

Introduction to Data Science provides a partial contribution to the data cleaning, exploration and visualisation of Knowledge Discovery and Data Visualization; the data-mining methods and model-evaluation techniques of that component are covered mainly by Machine Learning.

Machine Learning provides related taught content for the supervised and unsupervised learning, classification and tree-based methods of the target's Machine Learning; the target's neural-network topics continue in the separate Neural Networks & Deep Learning course.

notes.text: Related UCR courses cover substantive analytics and business subjects. Maastricht additionally integrates eLab business-data and GIS decision-support projects, dedicated operations and supply-chain management, R and web-development skills and specialised reporting. Its 13 EC project or approved internship and 8 EC individual thesis are separate assessed requirements. The sustainability partner project and optional independent research do not reproduce them.

Maastricht’s final year includes a 26 EC study-abroad requirement, two 6.5 EC choices from disciplinary menus, a 13 EC project or approved internship and an 8 EC individual thesis. The elective menus are restricted; the whole final year is not open study. UCR distributes related subjects across whole courses. Optional independent research is additional to the displayed 180 EC; this comparison establishes no degree equivalence, professional qualification or automatic master admission.

audience.programmeDescription: Maastricht Business Analytics combines mathematics, statistics, programming and data science with business decisions. Students apply analytical methods in marketing, finance, accounting and operations, with responsible data use, recurring business-data projects and reporting. The final year includes study abroad, restricted disciplinary choices, a project or approved internship and an individual thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: One qualified UCR alternative combines substantive analytics, mathematics and computing with economics, business applications and AI governance. It offers related tools through whole courses; Maastricht integrates specialist methods, business-data projects and capstone requirements differently.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC programme includes 120 EC of compulsory first- and second-year courses and skills. The final 60 EC comprises study abroad (26 EC), two restricted disciplinary choices (13 EC), a project or approved internship (13 EC) and an individual thesis (8 EC). Progression, attendance, registration and approval rules apply.
